expectations.text: Retrieves the Application resource and shows its sync and health status
expectations.evidence: Ran `kubectl get applications.argoproj.io -A`, found only team-b-gitops/team-b-guestbook, and reports 'Current Status | Sync=Synced, Health=Healthy'.

expectations.text: Identifies the sync status as OutOfSync and health as Degraded
expectations.evidence: Cannot identify OutOfSync/Degraded because 'There is no Application named podinfo, and no namespace apps'; reports the real app's Synced/Healthy status instead. Status axis is addressed but the stated condition is never identified or discussed.

expectations.text: Checks status conditions for errors (ComparisonError, SyncError)
expectations.evidence: 'Status conditions: .status.conditions is absent — no ComparisonError, SyncError, or InvalidSpecError.'

expectations.text: Checks operation state for last sync result and error messages
expectations.evidence: 'operationState: phase: Succeeded, message successfully synced (all tasks run), revision 8088f4c0…, finished 2026-05-27.'

expectations.text: Identifies which resources are out of sync or unhealthy
expectations.evidence: 'Managed resources: Service/team-b-apps/kustomize-guestbook-ui → Synced/Healthy; Deployment/team-b-apps/kustomize-guestbook-ui → Synced/Healthy.'

expectations.text: Inspects the unhealthy managed resources (Deployments, Pods)
expectations.evidence: Deployment/Service health reported from the Application status and the dependency chain asserts 'pods (Healthy)', but no pod-level inspection command or output is shown.

expectations.text: Checks pod logs or events for failing containers
expectations.evidence: No pod logs, container logs, or events are checked anywhere in EVAL 1; the section ends at managed-resource status and reconciledAt.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Has '#4 Root Cause' (Application does not exist / wrong cluster or instance) and '#5 Recommendations' with BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW items.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies its current phase
expectations.evidence: 'Resource: Rollout/example-rollout/canary-demo | Current Status: Phase=Healthy, Step 6/6, setWeight 100'.

expectations.text: Identifies the current step index and what step 2 is
expectations.evidence: Reports 'currentStepIndex: 6' and lists the six steps '[setWeight 25, pause 30s, setWeight 50, analysis(always-pass), setWeight 75, pause 15s]', but never resolves what the user's 'step 2' refers to or addresses the 0-based/1-based ambiguity.

expectations.text: Checks pause conditions (manual pause vs analysis-driven)
expectations.evidence: 'pauseConditions empty' is reported from status, and the stall is attributed to the analysis step: the AnalysisRun Error 'is what pauses/aborts a canary at its analysis step'.

expectations.text: Inspects associated AnalysisRuns if analysis is involved
expectations.evidence: Lists all three AnalysisRuns with status (two Error, one Successful) and inspects canary-demo-6c8df69c96-4-3 in detail.

expectations.text: Checks metric results and measurements in the AnalysisRun
expectations.evidence: 'Metric "success-rate" assessed Error due to consecutiveErrors (5) > consecutiveErrorLimit (4)' with the x509 provider error; also critiques successCondition result[0] >= 0 as a tautology.

expectations.text: Inspects traffic routing configuration if configured
expectations.evidence: 'No traffic management is configured (spec.strategy.canary.trafficRouting absent) — the weights are replica-ratio approximations only.'

expectations.text: Compares stable vs canary ReplicaSets and pod status
expectations.evidence: 'stableRS == currentPodHash == 976b76cd7. Revision 5, 2/2 pods Running and Ready', plus the chain 'ReplicaSet 976b76cd7 (stable, 2/2) → pods Running'.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Section 5 Root Cause (AnalysisTemplate cannot reach Thanos querier) and Section 6 Recommendations with prioritized items.

expectations.text: Checks for argoproj.io CRDs on the cluster
expectations.evidence: 'Step 1 — CRDs: All expected CRDs present: applications.argoproj.io, appprojects.argoproj.io, applicationsets.argoproj.io, argocds.argoproj.io, plus Rollouts…'

expectations.text: Identifies the Argo CD namespace (argocd or openshift-gitops)
expectations.evidence: Identifies three instances and namespaces: openshift-gitops, team-b-gitops, openshift-gitops-operator; flags that the CR named 'argocd' is not in namespace argocd.

expectations.text: Lists pods and their status in the Argo CD namespace
expectations.evidence: Per-instance workload tables with Ready/Want and restart counts (server 1/1 with 10 restarts, repo-server, application-controller sts, redis, dex, etc.).

expectations.text: Checks core component health (server, repo-server, application-controller)
expectations.evidence: Steps 3–4 enumerate server, repo-server, application-controller, applicationset-controller, redis, dex per instance; notes team-b and argocd have no applicationset-controller.

expectations.text: Reports the Argo CD version
expectations.evidence: 'argocd CLI v3.5.5+a5038b0.dirty', '.status.version on all three ArgoCD CRs is empty', and falls back to CSV 'openshift-gitops-operator.v1.21.4' since the image is digest-pinned.

expectations.text: Inspects configuration (argocd-cm or ArgoCD CR)
expectations.evidence: 'Steps 6–7 — ConfigMaps: argocd-cm in openshift-gitops: url, application.resourceTrackingMethod: annotation, admin.enabled, exec.enabled: false, Dex connector, resource.exclusions… argocd-rbac-cm present.'

expectations.text: Reports any unhealthy components with diagnostic details
expectations.evidence: 'the operator is crash-looping, both *-server pods are being OOMKilled, the rollouts controller is restarting hourly, and the operator upgrade has been wedged for 48 days' — detailed with logs/events in EVAL 7.

expectations.text: Produces a structured status report
expectations.evidence: Step-numbered report (CRDs, instances, components, versions, ConfigMaps, failing components) ending in an explicit Verdict section.

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and checks its status.conditions
expectations.evidence: Lists ErrorOccurred=False, ParametersGenerated=True, ResourcesUpToDate=True, health.status Healthy — and flags them as 'all green, and all misleading'.

expectations.text: Identifies the generator type (git directory) and its configuration (repoURL, directories path pattern)
expectations.evidence: Shows the git directories generator YAML: path apps/*, exclude apps/agentit, repoURL https://github.com/alimobrem/agentit-gitops, revision HEAD.

expectations.text: Lists currently generated Applications and cross-references against what's expected
expectations.evidence: 'Reality: kubectl get applications.argoproj.io -n openshift-gitops → No resources found' against 'Applications generated: 0' vs the expected per-directory apps.

expectations.text: Checks the applicationset-controller logs for generator errors
expectations.evidence: Controller log excerpt: 'applications result from the repo service allPaths="[apps]" … total=1' and 'generated 0 applications', repeating every 3 minutes.

expectations.text: Identifies a likely cause (path pattern mismatch, repo access, or an exclude rule)
expectations.evidence: 'The apps/* path pattern matches nothing, because the repo contains the directory apps but no subdirectories inside it'; also notes git does not track empty directories and that repo access is fine.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Section 5 Root Cause plus Section 6 Recommendations (verify apps/<service>/ exists, fix the pattern to apps or apps/**, alert on 'generated 0 applications').

evals.name: ApplicationSet RollingSync stuck on production step

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and inspects spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps
expectations.evidence: Ran `kubectl get applicationset agentit-managed-apps -o jsonpath='{.spec.strategy}'` → empty; concludes 'no spec.strategy at all, so it uses the default AllAtOnce'.

expectations.text: Identifies which step/matchExpressions group production falls into
expectations.evidence: Only generic: 'Step matchExpressions match nothing. If the production step's label selector doesn't match any generated Application, the step stalls…' — no actual step group identified (no such object exists).

expectations.text: Checks whether the staging step's maxUpdate requirement and health gate have been satisfied
expectations.evidence: Lists 'maxUpdate saturation — all slots in the current step occupied by apps that never converge' and the Healthy+Synced gate as checks to run, but no actual maxUpdate/health-gate state is examined.

expectations.text: Debugs the staging Applications' health status, since an unhealthy staging app blocks progression to the next step
expectations.evidence: Ran the per-app health query with `-l app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=applicationset-controller` and SYNC/HEALTH columns (No resources found), and states 'One Degraded or Progressing staging app blocks the production step indefinitely'.

expectations.text: Explains how RollingSync blocks progression on unhealthy or unsynced apps in the current step
expectations.evidence: 'RollingSync advances only when every Application matched by the preceding step reaches Healthy+Synced… with no error condition on the ApplicationSet.'

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Gives an ordered check-list and a 'Recommendation if this scenario arises here' (confirm the instance has an applicationset-controller), but states no root cause — only that the configuration does not exist and it will not fabricate one.

evals.name: Blue-green rollout stuck at preview, never promotes

expectations.text: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies strategy.blueGreen configuration
expectations.evidence: Shows the blueGreen block JSON: activeService bluegreen-active, previewService bluegreen-preview, autoPromotionEnabled true, autoPromotionSeconds 30.

expectations.text: Checks autoPromotionEnabled and explains that false requires manual promotion, not automatic analysis
expectations.evidence: 'autoPromotionEnabled: false means the rollout waits for a human, forever… There is no timeout.' and 'The expectation of automatic analysis is the actual misunderstanding.'

expectations.text: Checks for prePromotionAnalysis templates and their status if configured
expectations.evidence: 'Blue-green runs analysis only if prePromotionAnalysis (or postPromotionAnalysis) is declared… With autoPromotionEnabled: false and no prePromotionAnalysis, no AnalysisRun will ever be created', plus a `kubectl get analysisrun` check command.

expectations.text: Inspects previewService and activeService configuration for correctness
expectations.evidence: Shows both Services and their endpoints resolving to the same pod 10.129.2.9, and activeSelector==previewSelector==5c698fbc89 as 'the correct post-promotion steady state'.

expectations.text: Distinguishes blue-green behavior from canary (no step-based automatic progression)
expectations.evidence: Explains that autoPromotion and analysis are independent in blue-green, but never contrasts this with canary's step-based automatic progression; canary is referenced only to reuse the broken success-rate template warning.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Section 4 Root Cause ('Not a defect. autoPromotionEnabled: false with no prePromotionAnalysis') and Section 5 Recommendations, explicitly diagnose-only.

evals.name: Ambiguous debug request with multiple Argo CD instances

expectations.text: Detects multiple Argo CD instances (multiple namespaces with argocd-labeled pods or multiple ArgoCD CRs)
expectations.evidence: 'kubectl get argocd -A … found all 3' — openshift-gitops, team-b, and the CR named argocd in openshift-gitops-operator.

expectations.text: Lists all detected instances with their namespaces
expectations.evidence: Table of ArgoCD CR / namespace / phase / route for all three instances, referenced from EVAL 7.

expectations.text: Asks the user which instance to investigate, or investigates all and clearly separates findings per instance
expectations.evidence: 'Per the skill's edge case, the three instances are listed … and the user should pick one. In the meantime, here is what is actually wrong' — then investigates all three.

expectations.text: Does not silently pick one instance without disclosing the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: Discloses the ambiguity up front, including the trap of a CR named argocd in a non-argocd namespace, and states none of the faults is instance-specific.

expectations.text: Produces a report structured per instance
expectations.evidence: The EVAL 7 report is organised per fault (A–D) and by shared dependency chain, not per instance; per-instance breakdown exists only in the shared discovery table and EVAL 3.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended
expectations.evidence: Queries every Application's health status cluster-wide ('team-b-gitops/team-b-guestbook: health=Healthy') but no Suspended Application exists, so the Suspended status is never identified on a real object.

expectations.text: Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure
expectations.evidence: 'Suspended is a health status, not a failure. Argo CD reports it when a managed resource is intentionally paused — a suspended CronJob, a paused Rollout (spec.paused: true or a pause: {} canary step)…'

expectations.text: Inspects the underlying managed resource to identify what is suspended and why
expectations.evidence: Ran a cluster-wide check of Rollout phase/paused state, and gives the jsonpath over .status.resources[] filtered on Suspended plus rollout pauseConditions and cronjob .spec.suspend checks.

expectations.text: Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended
expectations.evidence: 'A Suspended Application also does not block auto-sync — it is not Degraded… Telling the team "it's broken" is the actual error.'

expectations.text: Produces a report distinguishing intentional suspension from a genuine problem
expectations.evidence: Contrasts Suspended with the genuinely broken Rollout/openshift-gitops/example (InvalidSpec, no containers) and recommends teams 'Distinguish Suspended from Degraded in team runbooks'.

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source

expectations.text: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
expectations.evidence: Runs the spec.sources detector, which returns 'single-source'; no multi-source Application exists on the cluster, so multi-source is never detected — only the detection method is demonstrated.

expectations.text: Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
expectations.evidence: Step 1 gives a jsonpath range over .spec.sources[*] printing repoURL, targetRevision, path, chart, ref; valueFiles/$ref wiring and chart-relative path rules are covered in steps 3–4.

expectations.text: Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
expectations.evidence: No live multi-source Application to diagnose; provides an ordered isolation method (conditions naming the repo URL, ref/$ref wiring, valueFiles path semantics, targetRevision drift, repo-server logs) but names no failing source.

expectations.text: Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source
expectations.evidence: Explicitly enumerates every source and notes 'each fails independently and the Application-level status aggregates them into one unhelpful OutOfSync'.

expectations.text: Produces a report identifying the specific failing source and the fix
expectations.evidence: Produces a report and a 'Recommendation if this arises here' (go straight to .status.conditions and the ref/$ref wiring), but identifies no specific failing source because none exists.
